newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on pre-holiday short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on pre-holiday short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Thursday in a sluggish, pre-holiday session, with short covering ahead of the extended weekend supporting the complex despite reports of softer cash.
August climbed 3.6 cents to close at $2.103 per million British thermal units. September settled 3.8 cents higher at $2.108. Other deferreds ended up by 2.8 to 3.9 cents.

"We saw a continuation of the (bullish) reaction to the storage numbers and some short covering ahead of the weekend," said one East Coast trader, adding prices may move higher next week because some end users likely went into July short gas.
NYMEX will be closed Friday for the Independence Day holiday.

Traders said a moderately bullish AGA number Wednesday helped set the stage for some pre-holiday shortcovering today, but they said forecasts for milder Northeast and Midwest weather next week should temper any bullish enthusiasm.

Temperatures next week in the Midwest and Northeast are expected to stay below-normal, with normal weather forecast for the Gulf Coast and Florida. Most of the West and west Texas are expected to remain hot.

AGA data showed U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 76 bcf, well below estimates in the 85-95 bcf range. Overall stocks are still 216 bcf, or 16 percent, over year-ago levels, but remain about 10 percent below the three year average.

Eastern storage gained 56 bcf last week and was 11 percent above last year, while producing region inventories remained 52 percent over 1996 levels. Western stocks continued to lag year-ago by nine percent.

Technically, traders still pegged August support at $2.055, the spot continuation low on June 12, with further buying likely at $2. Resistance was seen at $2.11, $2.15 and then along the down trendline at about $2.26-2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices were down slightly to the $2.06-2.11 area. Midcon pipes slipped a few cents to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate weekend gas was quoted a couple of cents lower in the mid-$2.30s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip gained 3.3 cents to $2.194. Hub open interest on July 2 rose 4,295 contracts to 198,431. NYMEX natgas volume figures were not available.
On the KCBT, August finished 2.2 cents higher at $1.972, while deferreds ended up by two to 4.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.4 cents to 13.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
